assertionCoverage.name: S6 trigger reclaims an EXPIRED running lease before attempting again
assertionCoverage.clause: A persisted expired running lease is moved to retry-pending before another attempt.
assertionCoverage.whyDirect: The trigger test seeds a durable running task with an expired lease, invokes the production trigger, and reads the stored task status.

assertionCoverage.name: S6 trigger reclaims an EXPIRED running lease before attempting again
assertionCoverage.clause: Lease recovery records the durable expired-lease reason.
assertionCoverage.whyDirect: The test reads the persisted failure code after the production trigger reclaims the old lease and asserts the canonical code.

assertionCoverage.name: S6 trigger reclaims an EXPIRED running lease before attempting again
assertionCoverage.expression: assert.ok(captured.input, 'the trigger must continue after reclaiming');
assertionCoverage.clause: An expired lease does not permanently block the next bounded attempt.
assertionCoverage.whyDirect: The production trigger test observes that the engine actually receives a new attempt after the expired task is reclaimed.

assertionCoverage.name: S6 trigger never steals a live lease
assertionCoverage.expression: assert.equal(captured.input, undefined, 'a live attempt must not be duplicated');
assertionCoverage.clause: An unexpired lease blocks a duplicate compaction attempt.
assertionCoverage.whyDirect: The trigger test seeds a live persisted lease and directly verifies that the production trigger does not call the engine a second time.

assertionCoverage.name: S6 trigger never steals a live lease
assertionCoverage.clause: A live lease remains running rather than being reclaimed speculatively.
assertionCoverage.whyDirect: The test reads the durable compaction row after trigger evaluation and observes that the existing running state is unchanged.

assertionCoverage.name: S6 trigger never steals a live lease
assertionCoverage.clause: The existing lease owner is preserved while its lease is live.
assertionCoverage.whyDirect: The assertion reads the persisted lease owner after the production trigger and verifies no ownership takeover occurred.

assertionCoverage.name: S6 trigger re-evaluates the durable lease after a store restart
assertionCoverage.clause: After the SQLite store is closed and reopened, persisted expired work is recovered as retry-pending.
assertionCoverage.whyDirect: The named test closes the real SQLite store, opens it again, invokes the production trigger, and reads the durable task status after recovery.

assertionCoverage.name: S6 trigger re-evaluates the durable lease after a store restart
assertionCoverage.clause: Restart recovery preserves the explicit expired-lease disposition.
assertionCoverage.whyDirect: The restarted trigger test reads the persisted failure code and directly verifies that recovery is based on the stored lease state.

assertionCoverage.name: S6 trigger re-evaluates the durable lease after a store restart
assertionCoverage.expression: assert.ok(captured.input, 'restart recovery must continue after reclaiming');
assertionCoverage.clause: The restarted trigger can continue the bounded attempt after reclaiming expired work.
assertionCoverage.whyDirect: The test observes an actual engine input after the store restart and lease recovery, proving the restart path does not silently discard the retry.
